sql:
SELECT COUNT(1) AS n
FROM   TPCDS_DB.store_sales ss
LEFT JOIN TPCDS_DB.promotion p ON ss.ss_promo_sk = p.p_promo_sk
WHERE  ss.ss_customer_sk IS NULL

attempts.sql: SELECT COUNT(1) AS n FROM TPCDS_DB.store_sales ss WHERE ss.ss_customer_sk IS NULL
attempts.change_summary: Removed the left outer join to promotion table as its columns are not referenced and the join does not affect row count since p_promo_sk is unique.

diagnosis.bottleneck: The query executes a left outer join to the promotion table that does not affect the final count (only store_sales rows are counted), yet it broadcasts the promotion table and performs a hash join, adding unnecessary broadcast and join overhead.

plan_nodes.note: LeftOuter BuildRight; Left keys [1]: [ss_promo_sk#57251]; Right keys [1]: [p_promo_sk#57276]; Join type: LeftOuter; Join

hypotheses.claim: A LEFT JOIN whose columns are never read still costs a join; if the joined key is unique it cannot change the rows and can be removed. (matched: left join tpcds_db.promotion p on ss.ss_promo_sk = p.p_promo_sk)

The left outer join is semantically redundant because the SELECT only counts rows from store_sales and never references promotion columns; removing the join would eliminate the broadcast hash join entirely.
Broadcasting the promotion table (300 rows) incurs serialization and network distribution cost; if the join were removed, this exchange would be unnecessary.
The partial aggregation processes rows that have passed through the join, increasing row width and hash table size; eliminating the join would reduce aggregation input size and CPU.
